signals.signal: RE-VERIFIED 01/08/2026 and corrected: SICAP's undocumented public JSON API works without login but ONLY if a Referer header is sent - without it the server returns HTTP 403 with body {"message":"Access Denied: Referrer cannot be null."}. Working calls: POST https://e-licitatie.ro/api-pub/NoticeCommon/GetCNoticeList/ with {"contractName":"<kw>","sysNoticeTypeIds":[],"pageSize":200,"pageIndex":0,"sortProperties":[]} (contract notices, returns estimated value, deadline and procedure state), and POST https://e-licitatie.ro/api-pub/DirectAcquisitionCommon/GetDirectAcquisitionList/ with {"directAcquisitionName":"<kw>"} (direct awards, returns the NAMED winner plus fiscal code, buyer and closing value). Two filters are silently ignored by the server and return the unfiltered 3,000-row cap: contractObject/contractTitle on GetCANoticeList (award notices) AND caNameFN on GetCNoticeList (contracting-authority name). Notice-detail endpoints getCNoticeById / getCNoticeV2 return HTTP 404 - the list endpoints are the only usable route.
signals.source_name: SICAP / e-licitatie.ro public API (api-pub), re-verified live
signals.implies: Repeatable no-login monitoring of the whole Romanian public demand pool for cash automation, POS acquiring, self-service and security - but buyer-name monitoring must be done by keyword, not by authority, and award winners above threshold must be sourced from TED instead.
signals.followup: Register both endpoints WITH the mandatory Referer header in the source-access registry; run a weekly keyword sweep; do not rely on caNameFN or GetCANoticeList filters.

signals.entity: DGRFP Ploiesti / DGRFP Brasov / Directia Fiscala Timisoara / DGITL Sector 3 (Romanian tax administration)
signals.signal: The Romanian tax administration is the single largest published public POS-acquiring demand pool. Recent frameworks: CN1089569 DGRFP Ploiesti 'Acord cadru privind servicii de acceptare a platilor, efectuate cu carduri de plata prin intermediul terminalelor POS', estimated RON 9,284,220, deadline 12/03/2026, status 'Atribuita' (awarded) - the largest single POS framework found; CN1090221 DGRFP Brasov payment-acceptance framework RON 2,170,000, awarded; SCN1173877 Directia Fiscala Timisoara card-and-cash collection over payment terminals RON 1,067,328, awarded; CN1093468 DGITL Sector 3 'Servicii de incasare a impozitelor si taxelor locale, prin card si numerar' RON 5,550,000, deadline 20/07/2026, still 'In desfasurare'; CN1092633 Directia Fiscala Brasov RON 1,100,000, deadline 23/06/2026, still 'In desfasurare'; CN1089852 DGRFP Ploiesti 'Acord cadru de servicii de casierie pentru trezoreriile statului organizate fara casierie tezaur' (outsourced cashier services for state treasuries with no vault) RON 4,953,000, deadline 24/03/2026, still 'In desfasurare'.
signals.source_name: SICAP contract notices CN1089569, CN1090221, SCN1173877, CN1093468, CN1092633, CN1089852
signals.implies: Aggregate published public POS/cash-acceptance demand well above RON 24m across these six procedures alone. The 'trezorerii fara casierie tezaur' cashier-outsourcing frameworks are the clearest self-service substitution opportunity in Romania: the state is paying banks to staff counters that a Printec cash recycler or assisted self-service kiosk could replace.
signals.likelihood: Rolling - each of the 8 regional DGRFPs re-tenders on a 2-4 year cycle
signals.followup: Pitch assisted self-service / cash recyclers to Ministry of Finance and the DGRFPs as an alternative to outsourced cashier headcount; obtain the CN1089569 award notice from TED to name the winning bank.

signals.signal: Banca Transilvania has near-monopoly capture of Romanian public-sector POS acquiring at direct-award level. In a sweep of SICAP direct acquisitions under CPV 66110000-4 published 01/05/2026-01/08/2026, Banca Transilvania is the named winner on the large majority of 'servicii bancare de acceptare carduri prin terminale POS' and SNEP/ghiseul.ro card-payment awards (examples: Spitalul Judetean de Urgenta Bacau DA40882688 RON 8,000, 24/07/2026; Directia Mobilitate Urbana Sector 4 DA40737312 RON 93,250, 01/07/2026; Autoritatea pentru Digitalizarea Romaniei DA40582226 RON 154,350, 09/06/2026; Primaria Targu Jiu DA40797346 RON 36,167.05, 09/07/2026). Other acquirers appear only occasionally: Banca Comerciala Romana (Oradea Transport Local DA40533130 RON 247,500, 02/06/2026; Consiliul Judetean Constanta DA40717602 RON 40,570), CEC Bank (Municipiul Brasov DA40840198 RON 166,600, 16/07/2026), Garanti Bank (Comuna Frumoasa), and non-bank players NETOPIA Financial Services and PayPoint Services (Compania APA Brasov DA40384197 RON 130,000 for cash/card bill collection via electronic equipment).
signals.implies: Any Printec POS/acquiring play in Romanian public sector must go THROUGH Banca Transilvania rather than around it - BT is the channel, not the competitor. Conversely the non-bank collectors (PayPoint, SelfPay, NETOPIA) show an unbundled cash/card acceptance market Printec could enter with self-service payment terminals.
signals.likelihood: Structural - unlikely to change in 12 months
signals.followup: Open a partner conversation with BT on terminal supply and managed services for its public-sector POS estate.

signals.signal: PRIMARY estate figures as at 31/03/2026 from BT's own interim report filed with the Bucharest Stock Exchange: the Bank operates 2,025 ATMs, 'din care 696 sunt masini multifunctionale' (of which 696 are multifunction machines, i.e. deposit-capable), plus 632 'terminale BT Express' used for operations other than cash dispensing, over 188,000 installed POS terminals, 47,000 STAR partner locations and over 8,400 e-commerce merchants. Digital-channel transactions rose 28% year on year; BT reports 5 million unique digitalised customers.
signals.source_name: Banca Transilvania S.A. interim financial report 31/03/2026, filed on BVB (TLV)
signals.implies: Only 696 of 2,025 BT ATMs (34%) are deposit-capable, so roughly 1,300 cash-out-only machines are candidates for recycler upgrade or replacement - the single largest identified self-service refresh pool in Romania. The 632 BT Express non-cash terminals confirm BT already runs a two-tier self-service estate that Printec kiosk/managed-services can extend.
signals.likelihood: Refresh cycles continuous; BT capex decisions annual
signals.followup: Build a BT account plan around recycler conversion of the ~1,300 dispense-only ATMs and managed services for the BT Express fleet; confirm the current ATM hardware incumbent.

signals.entity: C.N. Posta Romana S.A. (fiscal code RO 427410)
signals.signal: RE-VERIFIED 01/08/2026 and EXTENDED: Posta Romana is a recurring annual buyer of banknote counting/verification equipment. DA40258980 'Masini de numarat si verificat bancnote', closing value RON 267,680, published 27/04/2026, won by EUTRON INVEST ROMANIA (RO 4096491); the identical purchase ran the year before as DA38117884, RON 259,560, 15/05/2025, same winner. On the sorter side DA34883230 supplied 'Sortere pentru procesat si verificat bancnote' for RON 257,000 on 22/01/2024 to ROPECO BUCURESTI (RO 4912700), and DA40059888 of 23/03/2026 awarded ROPECO the maintenance and repair of those 12 banknote sorters for RON 54,064. Posta Romana also has two larger open procedures: CN1092504 maintenance and repair of electronic security systems (intruder detection subsystem etc.), estimated RON 3,662,000, deadline 29/06/2026, status 'In desfasurare'; and SCN1176522 'Saci medii si mari pentru procesare numerar' (medium and large cash-processing bags), RON 1,122,960, deadline 06/07/2026.
signals.source_name: SICAP direct-acquisition records DA40258980, DA38117884, DA34883230, DA40059888 and contract notices CN1092504, SCN1176522
signals.implies: Posta Romana runs a real cash centre with a 12-sorter installed base and buys counters annually - a natural Printec target for cash recyclers, teller automation and managed service. Both incumbents (Eutron Invest, Ropeco) are Romanian resellers rather than OEM-direct, so displacement is a distribution question, not a technology one. The RON 3.66m security-systems maintenance framework shows the same buyer also outsources multi-year technical service.
signals.likelihood: Next counter lot expected around April-May 2027 on the observed annual cadence; sorter fleet due for renewal (bought 2024)
signals.followup: Map Posta Romana's cash-centre sites and the expiry of the Ropeco sorter maintenance contract; propose recycler-based counter automation ahead of the 2027 buy.

SelfPay: Directia Generala de Evidenta a Persoanelor Sector (fiscal code 29481212) rented 'Statie de Plata SelfPay cu functii acceptare plati card bancar si numerar' twice - DA40515730, RON 77,140, 29/05/2026 and DA40650522, RON 15,428, 17/06/2026. signals.implies: Romania already accepts kiosk-as-a-service commercial models in the public sector, and a state bank (CEC) has endorsed one. That validates a Printec managed-self-service / kiosk-rental proposition in Romania and identifies SelfPay as the incumbent to displace or partner with - it is also the operator that Printec's Greek Cashflex/KEA off-site ATM model most closely resembles.
signals.likelihood: Expanding - repeat orders visible within 3 weeks at one buyer
signals.followup: Size the SelfPay estate in Romania and assess partner-versus-compete; test a Printec kiosk-rental offer with a municipal or utility buyer.

coverage_notes: RECOVERY PASS on Romania SEAP/SICAP. Read the orphaned checkpoint at parts/2026-08-01_run1-orphaned-backup/romania-seap-sicap.json (3 signals) and RE-VERIFIED all three against the live primary source on 01/08/2026: (1) the api-pub access route was re-verified AND CORRECTED - the earlier note omitted that a Referer header is mandatory (plain POST returns 403 'Access Denied: Referrer cannot be null.') and I additionally established that the caNameFN authority filter is silently ignored and that the notice-detail endpoints 404; (2) CEC Bank cec.ro/achizitii re-fetched with a desktop UA, still HTTP 200 and still only the same two closed procedures - confirmed unchanged; (3) the two Posta Romana direct awards were re-verified record-by-record and EXTENDED with the prior-year repeat DA38117884 (15/05/2025, RON 259,560, same winner) and the original sorter supply DA34883230 (22/01/2024, RON 257,000, Ropeco), which turns a one-off into a documented annual cadence. Beyond recovery, I swept SICAP across ~48 Romanian and English keyword sets (bancomat, automat bancar, masina de numarat bancnote, sortere, terminale POS, plata cu cardul, chiosc self-service, automat de plata, seif, tezaur, casierie, transport valori, procesare numerar, sisteme de securitate, antiefractie, control acces, HSM, personalizare carduri, identificare video, spalarea banilor, antifrauda and others) over both the contract-notice and direct-acquisition endpoints, then filtered to publications from 2025-09 onward. That surfaced the material TED does NOT carry: BNR's below-threshold HSM support award (SCN1172961) and its cancelled CIT-fleet GPS procedure (SCN1172275), DEER's cancelled RON 27.05m PKI-HSM procurement, the tax administration's POS and treasury-cashier frameworks, Posta Romana's security-maintenance framework, and CFR Calatori's recurring CIT lots. I cross-checked BNR CN1093831 (RON 3,438,026.83, deadline 06/08/2026) against the TED unit's figure - it matches exactly and no erratum has been filed. On the bank side I went to primary filings rather than press: BT's interim report for 31/03/2026 on BVB was downloaded and text-extracted locally with pdfminer, yielding 2,025 ATMs / 696 multifunction / 632 BT Express / 188,000+ POS. GENUINE GAPS: named winners for the above-threshold POS frameworks (CN1089569, CN1090221) could not be retrieved because the SICAP award-notice endpoint ignores its title filter - these must come from TED award notices, which sit with the TED unit. BCR and BRD publish no procurement portal and neither appeared as a buyer anywhere in the SICAP sweep, so no BCR/BRD tender signal exists to report; BCR appears only as an acquiring bank winning municipal POS direct awards. A search result from aggregator business-talks.ro asserting that Banca Transilvania integrated BRD was checked against BT's own newsroom and is FALSE - the actual 2026 transaction is BT's acquisition of BRD Pensii (pension manager), not the bank; it is not a tender signal and is recorded here only so the claim is not re-derived next run.
access_issues: SICAP api-pub returns HTTP 403 with body {"message":"Access Denied: Referrer cannot be null."} unless a Referer header is supplied; resolved by sending Referer/Origin plus a desktop User-Agent. GetCANoticeList (award notices) silently ignores its contractObject/contractTitle filter and GetCNoticeList silently ignores caNameFN, both returning the unfiltered 3,000-row cap - so authority-scoped and award-winner queries are not possible through this API and were worked around with keyword filtering. The notice-detail endpoints https://e-licitatie.ro/api-pub/PublicNotice/getCNoticeById/<id> and .../getCNoticeV2/<id> both return HTTP 404; the public notice pages are an Angular SPA and are not fetchable as text, so all notice data here comes from the list endpoints. https://www.cec.ro/achizitii returns 403 to the plain fetch tool but 200 with a desktop User-Agent (route used). https://www.bancatransilvania.ro/news/comunicate-de-presa/... returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch; worked around by using the BVB-filed interim report PDF instead and extracting it locally with pdfminer.six.
operator_requests: TED award notices for SICAP procedures CN1089569 (DGRFP Ploiesti POS framework, RON 9,284,220, awarded) and CN1090221 (DGRFP Brasov, RON 2,170,000, awarded) - needed to name the winning acquiring banks, and not retrievable through the SICAP API because its award-notice filter is broken. Also the full tender dossier for BNR SCN1172961 (HSM support services, RON 335,490, awarded) if an operator has a SICAP login, to identify the incumbent HSM vendor and contract expiry.
